newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dlr gains vs yen as bond yield hit low in Tokyo.
newsitem.headline: Dlr gains vs yen as bond yield hit low in Tokyo.

text.p: *Dollar edged up against yen in morning Tokyo as key 182nd 10-year bond Japanese government bond (JGB) yield fell to all-time record low of 2.065 percent, dealers said.
*200-day moving average near 118.25 yen seen to be next resistance point, they added.
*Exporter offers, which were left before they entered their summer break, may appear above 118.50 yen.
*Mark/yen also rose in tandem after earlier easing slightly on profit-taking.
*No substantial mark offers against yen from exporters detected so far, a dealer at a Japanese trust bank said.
*Mark was traded around 64.02/05 yen at 0132 GMT.
*"It is still hard to know whether the mark will turn around now and fall," the trust bank dealer said.
0015 GMT --*Dollar capped versus yen in early Tokyo on Friday due to light profit-taking, but maintained overnight gains due to persistent buying demand by interbank operators.
*Mark also fell slightly against yen on profit-taking after rising sharply above 64.12 yen overnight.

*"Interbank dealers are eager to pick up dollars on dips following unexpected rallies against the yen overnight," said a spot dealer at a Japanese city bank. "But we are a bit cautious about buying aggressively now ahead of the release of Japanese trade data on Monday."
*Underlying dollar sentiment improved rapidly after speculative and technical buying led by U.S. fund operators pushed up dollar versus yen.
*Dealers said there was a wide variety of yen-selling speculation, including worries about the economic recovery in Japan, which pushed down the yen overnight.
